story.title: Binance Recovers 90% of Stolen Cryptocurrency Assets After Hack
story.summary: Binance has announced that it has replenished approximately 90% of the cryptocurrency assets stolen during a recent security incident. The exchange confirmed that the majority of the stolen funds have been recovered following the hack.

timeline_highlights.title: Massive $6.3 Billion Hack Targets Binance Cryptocurrency Exchange
timeline_highlights.summary: Hackers have stolen approximately $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, marking it as potentially the largest crypto heist in history. Analysts suggest that the attack may have been orchestrated by North Korean hackers. In response to the breach, Binance has stated that it will cover the losses and has frozen about half of the stolen assets to mitigate the impact on users.
key_facts: This incident is considered the largest crypto hack ever.
Experts suspect North Korean involvement in the attack.
Binance has pledged to cover the losses and freeze some stolen assets.

explore_lenses.label: Does “replenished” mean the crypto was recovered?
explore_lenses.title: Coverage is not the same as recovery
explore_lenses.summary: Binance says it has replaced about 90% of the value affected, chiefly by deploying its own resources; that is distinct from retrieving assets from the attacker. The difference matters because customers’ balances may be made whole even if much of the stolen crypto remains under criminal control.

claims.text: Binance said it had covered 90% of the hacked loss using a partial SAFU deployment, part of its Futures insurance fund, and its corporate treasury.

Binance previously said roughly $3 billion of an estimated $6.3 billion impact had been frozen on-chain, indicating that the reported replenishment includes replacement funds rather than solely recovered assets.

Binance’s stated position is that it—not users—will absorb the financial loss, while it works with law enforcement, token issuers, blockchain-intelligence firms and other exchanges to trace and recover frozen assets.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: Binance has not publicly established how much of the frozen amount will ultimately be returned, forfeited, or remain inaccessible.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about how the breach happened?
explore_lenses.title: The root cause remains under investigation
explore_lenses.summary: Binance’s preliminary account centers on unauthorized withdrawal transactions enabled through compromised internal access, but the company says it later found further breach points. A private blockchain-intelligence firm has attributed the attack to a North Korean unit, while Binance has not published a completed forensic report or cited a government attribution.

claims.text: Binance’s initial investigation said a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop may have let an attacker access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawals; it said it had found no evidence of leaked wallet private keys.
In its subsequent update, Binance said it had uncovered additional points of breach and would publish technical findings only after verification and without compromising the investigation.

TRM Labs attributes the theft to TraderTraitor, which it describes as a North Korean state-sponsored unit, with high confidence; that is an analyst attribution rather than a publicly reported government finding.

explore_lenses.label: What needs to happen before normal service returns?
explore_lenses.title: Proof and withdrawal restoration are the next tests
explore_lenses.summary: The next immediate measures are a completed proof-of-reserves verification and a phased restoration of withdrawals. These are Binance targets, not yet completed outcomes as of October 31, 2026.

claims.text: Binance says ten major assets—BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC—are fully backed, while the remaining 10% consists of less-liquid tokens it is still buying through market and over-the-counter channels.

Binance took a proof-of-reserves snapshot at 00:00 UTC on October 31 and said the full zero-knowledge proof should allow holders of the ten listed tokens to independently check at least 1:1 backing once generated.
Forecast: Binance said it expected the full zero-knowledge proof by November 3, 2026 UTC and remained on track to reopen withdrawals on November 1, 2026, subject to confirmation and security checks.

story_report.summary: Binance says it has replenished 90% of cryptocurrency assets lost in a security incident, using a mix of its Secure Asset Fund for Users, Futures insurance fund and corporate treasury. The exchange said it, rather than customers, would absorb the financial loss while it seeks to trace and recover assets frozen on-chain. The announcement describes replacement of customer backing, not solely the recovery of stolen cryptocurrency, as Binance continues to obtain the remaining less-liquid tokens.

sections.heading: Binance Funding and Asset Recovery
sections.body: Binance previously said that about $3 billion of an estimated $6.3 billion impact had been frozen on-chain. It has not said how much of those frozen assets will ultimately be returned or otherwise recovered. The exchange said it is working with law enforcement, token issuers, blockchain-intelligence firms and other exchanges to trace the funds, while maintaining that users will not bear the loss.

sections.heading: Binance Investigation of the Breach
sections.body: Binance’s initial investigation said a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop may have enabled an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawals. It said it had found no evidence that wallet private keys were leaked, but later reported finding additional breach points. Separately, TRM Labs attributed the theft with high confidence to TraderTraitor, which it describes as a North Korean state-sponsored unit; this is an analyst assessment, not a publicly reported government finding.

sections.heading: Binance Reserves and Withdrawal Plans
sections.body: Binance said BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC are fully backed, while it buys the remaining 10% in less-liquid tokens through market and over-the-counter channels. It took a proof-of-reserves snapshot at 00:00 UTC on October 31 and said a full zero-knowledge proof would allow holders of the listed assets to verify at least 1:1 backing. Binance said it expected the proof by November 3, 2026 UTC and was targeting a November 1, 2026 reopening of withdrawals, subject to security checks.

unresolved.text: The full attack sequence, all compromised systems, the identity of those responsible, and whether private keys or additional customer systems were affected have not been publicly resolved.

It remains unresolved whether the proof-of-reserves process and withdrawal reopening will proceed on the stated timetable, and whether Binance can source the remaining less-liquid tokens without disruption.

related_stories.title: BJP Criticizes Opposition's Mock Parliament and Challenges Gandhi to Debate
related_stories.summary: The BJP has criticized the opposition's mock Parliament initiative, with MP Sambit Patra suggesting that Rahul Gandhi should be made a 'mock PM.' Patra dismissed the opposition's allegations of electoral fraud, citing that similar events occurred during Congress rule. Additionally, Home Minister Amit Shah has challenged Gandhi to debate the allegations of vote theft in Parliament, coinciding with an upcoming opposition rally in Delhi.

related_stories.title: UK Prime Minister Open to Slavery Apology Amid Caribbean Tour
related_stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has expressed openness to a formal apology for Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade. This statement comes as King Charles continues his tour of the Caribbean, where discussions about the UK's colonial history are prominent. However, Burnham has ruled out the possibility of financial reparations, despite ongoing demands from Caribbean nations.
